assumptions: Data covers April–August 2008 for one online clothing shop; it is a workflow demonstration and NOT evidence of present-day shopping behavior.
In this file session_id is globally unique, but the contract does not assume that: the composite session_key is authoritative.
Coded columns (country, colour, location, etc.) are categorical ids, not quantities; only price/order/day are treated as ordered numbers.

Code meanings (category/colour/location/pose/price-2/country labels) come from the dataset description at docs/reference/e-shop_clothing_2008_data_description.txt and are transcribed into a display-only codebook; they are NOT validation constraints.
One row (2008-04-10, session 2766, click 27) is labeled category 2 (skirts) but carries product code A18 (the A/trousers family): a single cross-column inconsistency, left as-is and not enforced.
cleaning_rules: Parse with delimiter ';' and UTF-8/ASCII encoding; the file uses CRLF line endings.
Normalize column names with normalize_column_name (lowercase, non-alphanumeric runs -> single underscore, trimmed).
Keep 'page 2 (clothing model)' as text; parse all other columns as int64.
Require zero nulls in every column (the source has none).
Reject full-row duplicates (the source has none).
Derive session_key = 'YYYY-MM-DD-s<session_id>' as the canonical session id.
Sort deterministically by (year, month, day, session_id, order) ascending (stable). This sort defines click order regardless of on-disk row order.
Require each session's 'order' values to form a contiguous 1..n sequence (no gaps, no duplicates).
constraints: A random row split is forbidden: clicks in a session are correlated and would leak across splits. Use the chronological month split below.
Features must use only the current and earlier clicks of the same session; no value derived from click t+1 or later may enter the features (target excepted).
All four main categories must be present in every split (verified: they are).

dataset.name: Clickstream Data for Online Shopping
dataset.publisher: Mariusz Łapczyński and Sylwester Białowąs (UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 553)

label_codebook.note: Human-readable value labels for DISPLAY ONLY; not a validation constraint. Generated from the data description.

schema.description: Calendar year of the click. Observed: constant 2008.
schema.name: year

schema.description: Month of the click. Documented + observed: 4=April … 8=August.
schema.name: month

schema.description: Click sequence within a session, starting at 1 (documented 'order'). Observed: a contiguous 1..n run per verified session.
schema.name: order

schema.description: Coded origin of the IP address (47 categories; 1–42 are countries, 12='unidentified', 43–47 are TLD groups .biz/.com/.int/.net/.org). Observed domain 1–47. Labels: see the codebook.
schema.name: country

schema.description: Per-session id (documented 'short record'). Observed 1–24026 and, in this file, globally unique; the canonical session key still composes it with the date (see session_key) so it stays correct if ids reset per day.
schema.name: session_id

schema.description: Main product category. Documented codes: 1=trousers, 2=skirts, 3=blouses, 4=sale. This is the source column for the prediction target.
schema.name: page_1_main_category

schema.description: Product code (documented: 217 products, no names in the source), e.g. 'A13'. Observed pattern letter+digits; the first letter (A/B/C/P) tracks the main category for all but 1 of 165,474 rows (one skirts row carries an A-code: 2008-04-10, session 2766, click 27).
schema.name: page_2_clothing_model

schema.description: Coded product colour. Documented 14-colour palette; observed domain 1–14.
schema.name: colour

schema.description: Photo location on the page (documented: screen split into six regions). Observed domain 1–6.
schema.name: location

schema.description: Model pose. Documented: 1=en face, 2=profile. Observed domain 1–2.
schema.name: model_photography

schema.description: Price in US dollars (documented). Observed integers 18–82; validated as a positive integer rather than a fixed set so it stays feature-friendly.
schema.name: price

schema.description: Whether the price is above the category average. Documented: 1=yes, 2=no. Observed domain 1–2.
schema.name: price_2

schema.description: Page number within the e-store (documented 1–5). Observed domain 1–5.
schema.name: page

session_key.rationale: Composite key is canonical so sessions stay distinct even if a bare session_id is reused on another day.

sort.policy: Click order within a session is defined by 'order'; rows are re-sorted deterministically regardless of on-disk order.

split.rationale: Sessions are correlated; a random row split leaks future clicks of a session into training. See docs/decisions/0001-no-random-row-split.md.

target.definition: Within the same verified session (sorted by 'order' ascending), the next click's page_1_main_category (shift(-1)).
target.name: next_main_category
